request.spec:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
The trim rule now applies once over the whole tree: the consolidated due-total and overdue-total
leave out the single highest and the single lowest person's figure over all people of the tree
when three or more have one, instead of adding up each sheet's trimmed total. The consolidated
people count counts each person once across the tree: people whose names or aliases match (as names
are compared) are one person.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The consolidated figures now follow the new rule, and `bin/e2e` passes all 4 tests in the spec. After that run I only re-wrapped a comment, with no code change.

The change is in the front end, which is where the consolidated figures were already worked out; the server and stored data didn't need to change.

- **Due-total and overdue-total:** each person's figure, as their row shows it, is gathered from every sheet in the tree. The single highest and single lowest are then left out once over the whole tree, when three or more people have a figure. Before, each sheet was trimmed and the results were added together. This is in `src/main/frontend/features/consolidated/consolidated.slot.tsx`, plus a small new helper in `rates/overdue.slot.tsx` that gives each person's overdue-total.
- **People count:** names and aliases are compared trimmed and ignoring case, the same way elsewhere in the app. People whose names or aliases match count as one person, and the matching carries through: if A matches B and B matches C, all three are one.

One thing to be aware of: two matching people still each put their own figure into the trim; their figures aren't added together first. The test data needs this. In the first test, "Ada" is on two sheets, and the expected due-total of 9.00 only comes out when her two figures are trimmed separately (merging them would give 7.00).

The per-grade due-totals and per-status counts are still added up sheet by sheet, as before.
